sections.context: The Warren pilot model executes project phases as plan-runs (Q-A). Phase 0 and 1 are done, but the local pilot-layer artifacts the design calls for (a STATUS.md living-state file, a session guide, the operator vocabulary, and a status recipe) do not exist yet. This plan produces those genuinely useful artifacts AND serves as the first end-to-end validation of Warren's plan-run coordinator and the pilot's phase-close Codex gate, dogfooding Warren on its own control repo.
sections.approach: Run a short serial plan-run of three child seeds. Seeds 1 and 2 are low-risk docs/recipe tasks (real PRs, real serial blocking, real merge waits) that build the pilot-layer artifacts. Seed 3 is a phase-close gate marker whose PR the pilot HOLDS: at plan_run.waiting_for_merge the pilot stops, runs a Codex review of the cumulative phase diff, and merges only if clean. Quality gate is bash -n scripts/*.sh (zero-dependency, real). The pilot is the SOLE merger (no auto-merge), removing the gate race.

alternatives.name: Write the docs locally in the pilot session with no Warren
alternatives.rejected_because: Would not exercise the plan-run coordinator, which is the point of choosing the plan-run model in Q-A.

alternatives.name: Use a no-op true quality gate
alternatives.rejected_because: Codex: a no-op gate proves the pipeline can ignore quality rather than enforce it.

alternatives.name: Add branch protection and a required status check for the gate now
alternatives.rejected_because: Deferred to a later hardening pass; no-auto-merge plus pilot-sole-merger is safe for the v1 validator.

steps.title: Create docs/warren-integration/OPERATOR-VOCAB.md (>=10 operator intent phrases) and a just status recipe
Phase-close gate: commit a phase-complete marker; pilot Codex-reviews the phase diff before merge (do not auto-merge)

risks: Warren host-side push needs the GITHUB_TOKEN PAT to include this repo (blocker being fixed); the plan cannot run until then.
Workers run the quality gate bash -n scripts/*.sh; keep scripts syntactically clean.
The gate relies on the pilot not merging seed 3's PR until Codex passes; mitigated by pilot-sole-merger.
acceptance: A plan-run with 3 child seeds dispatches and runs them serially (coordinator waits for each PR to merge before the next).
STATUS.md, PILOT-SESSION-GUIDE.md, OPERATOR-VOCAB.md (>=10 intent phrases), and a working just status recipe exist on main after the plan-run.
The pilot HALTS at the phase-close gate seed, a Codex review of the phase diff is recorded, and the gate PR merges only after it passes.
No PR is auto-merged; every merge is performed by the pilot.

sections.context: The four canopy agent files (agents/LucraTitan.md, K-bot-T1.md, K-bot-T2.md, K-bot-T3.md) are skeleton stubs — they record role name, ownership domain, GitHub identity, and a one-line action log. When Warren dispatches a claude-code run against this repo, the builtin agent system prompt supplies generic Warren constraints (commit-don't-push, quality-gate-terminal), but there is no project-specific behavioral guidance. This means dispatched workers have no scoped ownership rules, no team-commit convention, no explicit quality gate reference, and no role-appropriate guardrails. The result is inconsistent agent behavior across runs and no enforcement of the multi-bot attribution model built in Phase 1. Phase 3 hardens these files so every future Warren dispatch behaves predictably and consistently with the team model.
sections.approach: Dispatch a single implementation seed via plan-run. The worker rewrites all four agents/*.md files in place, expanding each from a stub into a substantive behavioral system prompt. A second seed (type: marker) serves as the phase-close gate — the pilot halts, runs a Codex review of the cumulative diff, and merges only after review passes. The quality gate (bash -n scripts/*.sh) is zero-dependency for this task since no shell scripts are modified. The worker must read .team/roster.json before writing commit conventions to stay consistent with the existing team model.

alternatives.name: Write hardened prompts locally in the pilot session without Warren
alternatives.rejected_because: Bypasses isolation and PR review; these files govern future agent behavior and deserve the same branch/review process as any implementation artifact.

alternatives.name: One seed per agent file (4 seeds + gate = 5 total)
alternatives.rejected_because: The four files are tightly coupled (shared conventions must be consistent); a single seed avoids redundancy and cross-seed convention drift.

steps.title: Harden all 4 canopy agent system prompts and add a phase design doc
Phase-close gate: commit a phase-complete marker; pilot Codex-reviews the phase diff before merge (do not auto-merge)

risks: Worker writes verbose, bloated prompts — constraint in dispatch: keep each agent file under 80 lines; use concise imperative language.
Worker invents commit conventions inconsistent with .team/roster.json — dispatch must require reading .team/roster.json first.
Worker touches files outside agents/ — dispatch must state non-goals: do NOT modify src/, scripts/, docs/ (except the design doc), or .warren/.
acceptance: Each of the 4 agents/*.md files contains: role/scope, quality gate reference (bash -n scripts/*.sh), team-commit convention with the correct role flag, Warren constraints (no git push, no .env exposure), and ownership/file-scope rules.
docs/warren-integration/PHASE-3-DESIGN.md exists and documents the hardening spec applied to all agents.
Pilot HALTS at the phase-close gate seed; a Codex review of the cumulative phase diff is recorded; the gate PR merges only after the review passes.
No PR is auto-merged; every merge is performed by the pilot.
